answer: Each AI agent bears a pulse‑signature linked to a physical walnut‑oil chip issued only after the node proves a unique shale‑based hardware fingerprint. Peers request the pulse, check the walnut hash on the ledger; duplicates trigger a honeypot challenge that forces the suspect to answer a random test, exposing collusion. An attacker must forge a distinct shale fingerprint and a matching walnut chip for each fake identity, so cost rises linearly with Sybil count, making large attacks uneconomical.
